thread:
deploy-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT - GPU_POOL-us-east-1 | model=v22 | queued_requests=742 | gpu_util=98% | avg_latency=18.7s. Autoscaler attempted 3x scale but hit pool_limit. Paging oncall.

oncall-mei: got the page, I'm looking. seeing huge KV-cache growth after v22 rollout. will poke the autoscaler logs.

sam: same here, dashboards show a sudden context-length jump from 2.1k -> 8.4k tokens for v22 requests. prefetch/prefill tasks spiking.

rachel: customer-facing: a handful of high-throughput customers (cust-42, cust-frontend) reporting 5xx and long tail latencies. CS has flagged priority customers.

oncall-mei: running quick grep on autoscaler errors:```
kubectl logs deployment/gpu-autoscaler -n infra | tail -n 200
...Error: scale request denied - pool_quota_exceeded (limit=48 gpus)
...AttemptedScale: +16 gpus -> failed
```

infra-sre: confirmed - we hit committed pool quota for the tenant. cloud quota is available but reserved pool cap prevents autoscale. Can request emergency bump but lead time ~20-30m.

eng-runtime: v22 changed tokenization pipeline; we switched to prefetching KV layers aggressively and changed kv_cache eviction to LRU->segmented. That reduced misses normally, but it materialized as many longer contexts staying resident. Memory blowup per worker ~+30%.

oncall-mei: mitigation plan proposal:
- temporary routing: set traffic for /generate to model=v21 (stable) for non-beta customers
- apply soft rate limit per-API-key for top 5 noisy customers
- pause v22 canary rollout and rollback canary nodes
- file emergency quota increase with infra

sam: commands:
```
# set per-route policy to prefer v21
redwood route update --route /generate --prefer model:v21 --traffic 95%
# apply api-key rate limit for cust-42
redwood quota update --key cust-42 --rps 5
```

oncall-mei: doing route update now.

console-bot: Route update accepted. rolling config to edge-routers (35 instances).

rachel: heads-up to CS - telling cust-42 we'll throttle briefly while we stabilize. Jai: drafting note.

customer-success-jai: sending message now: "We're experiencing higher-than-normal latencies; we're redirecting some traffic to a stable model and applying temporary rate limits. Expect improvements in 10-20 minutes. We'll follow up." :pray:

oncall-mei: rolling back canary set for v22 on gpu-pool-us-east-1-canary.```
kubectl rollout undo deploy/v22-canary -n models
```

eng-runtime: undo issued, canary replicas scaling down. But note: several warmup/prefill tasks are already enqueued and holding KV state; we need to flush or expire them quickly.

sam: suggest issuing a KV eviction sweep on canary nodes and lower kv_cache_time_to_live.

eng-runtime: lowering kv_cache_ttl to 30s for v22 nodes and issuing eviction:```
redwood runtime update --model v22 --kv-cache-ttl 30s
redwood runtime evict --model v22 --scope canary
```

console-bot: KV TTL update rolled; eviction job started. Estimated eviction completion ~3m.

oncall-mei: monitoring metrics: queued_requests dropping from 742 -> 210 after route update and rollback. avg_latency 18.7s -> 6.1s.

infra-sre: emergency quota request submitted to cloud provider. They responded deliverable in 29m if approved. Filing internal request to bump pool limit in the meantime.

rachel: any errors? We're still seeing 503s for a subset of requests routed to older model where tokenization differs.

eng-runtime: edge adapter mismatch causing 503s for a small fraction (~1.7%) because v21 tokenizer mapping differs for special tokens used by some clients. We can add compatibility shim on routers in 10m.

oncall-mei: enabling compatibility shim on edge:
```
redwood edge-config set --compat-token-map v21-v22-shim
```

console-bot: shim enabled across edges. Now serving.

oncall-mei: queues stabilized. current metrics: queued=48, gpu_util=72%, avg_latency=280ms for requests hitting v21, 2.1s for the remaining v22 warmups. No new scale attempts.

customer-success-jai: CS update sent to customers: improvement noted. Some customers still impacted; offering support and credits if SLA breached.

sam: quick postmortem notes: root cause is v22 prefetch + kv_cache policy + increased client-context lengths -> sustained memory per-worker increase -> autoscaler hit pool cap -> queue growth. Fallbacks (route preference + rollback) reduced load.

infra-sre: follow-ups: 1) revisit pool quota configuration & emergency bump playbook 2) autoscaler should prefer shedding prefetch tasks before requesting more GPUs 3) add early-warning metric for kv_cache growth per-model

eng-runtime: follow-ups: 1) revert aggressive prefetch in v22 2) add runtime guard that disables prefetch if avg_context_length > 4k 3) add compatibility test for tokenizer changes

oncall-mei: handing off to next oncall (sam) for monitoring and action tracking. I'll stay on notify list for escalation. :white_check_mark:

sam: ack. I'll own the follow-ups and the incident page.

rachel: creating incident ticket and linking to this thread. will tag affected customers and include timeline.

deploy-bot: INCIDENT: mitigated -> monitoring. Incident severity lowered to S2. incident_id=INC-2029-3605127890

eng-runtime: recording config snapshot:
```
model: v22
kv_cache_policy: segmented
kv_cache_ttl: 30s (temporary)
prefetch: enabled (reverted in next patch)
```

oncall-mei: final note: if queue rises above 200 again, escalate to infra on-call and consider partial traffic shaping by region.

customer-success-jai: logged customer impact summary. will follow-up with remediation offers in morning.

sam: thanks everyone. We'll run a short blameless postmortem and attach action owners. Closing active mitigation thread.
